cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the sharing moves at the size it should.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Choose the heading you want this week and hold it for three days — no spread, no yes to every request that arrives.
cells.core:
When someone close to you is short of something, your hands already know the right amount to pass over. Not a rescue, not a token — just what this person can carry and what you can spare. You don't make a project of it. What you pass along holds because it was sized to the person, not to the volume of the need, and the ones on the receiving end can feel the difference.

Before the next request sets your direction, choose the heading from what you want, not from the logic of who sounds most desperate. Hold that line for three days. Saying yes to each request that comes means no direction at all. One clear line beats an even spread — that is what this clearing is asking of you.

cells.tense: You are bracing against an ending that hasn't happened, and you are the one holding the door.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Pay one small debt you know is real, quietly, and notice which account stops asking once it is settled.
cells.core:
Here the sharing has gone past measure. Something is being kept alive that already finished — a role, a standing obligation, a way of holding it together — and the cost is being paid by your body, quietly. You give where you think you still owe, when nothing is owed, and the shape of it gets harder to keep in view. The tally runs on in you and it is not producing fairness, only heat, and the ones near you can feel that heat without knowing its source.

Settle the small account that is actually yours. Pay the one debt that is real, and leave the ones that only exist in your arithmetic alone — that is the fair call here, not the tidy one. Watch what happens to the tally once one line is closed.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed a while back, and you haven't noticed.
cells.act: release the method, not the purpose
cells.ask: Drop one way you have been showing up for people that has stopped landing, and keep the caring itself.
cells.core:
Something came to an end here, and what you are doing now is insisting on the old form of it. The strength is still in you. Nothing moves from you to anyone, because the way you used to hand it over no longer fits where you are. There is no lack of resources — there is a grip on one method that has finished its work.

What gets released is not the caring, it is the one approach. Drop what isn't landing any more, and try one different version this week, once, with one person. If the new shape lands, you'll know what the old one was hiding. Keep the purpose; let the method go.
cells.sheetLine: It stopped moving because you're holding the old shape.

cells.tense: You are already writing in this room, and your account has the pen elsewhere.
cells.act: decide the heading from what you want, not from logic
cells.ask: Before the next request sets your direction, decide where you actually want to head — and make a choice from there.
cells.core:
The endings have been happening — a role finished, a phase closed, an arrangement fallen away — and your telling calls it circumstances. Somebody cleared that room, and it was you. The direction the clearing points is yours, made out of your own want, and your version leaves you out of it. You describe yourself as the one who happened to be there when it happened.

Steer by something you actually want, before the next request sets your heading for you. Decide where you want to head — on paper, or to yourself — and make a choice this week from that want rather than from who needs what. Your direction is what kept the ground under theirs. Own that, and the room stays yours.
